title: Using piggyBac transposon gene expression vectors to transfect Zscan5b gene into mouse pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Prepare cell culture plates; 12-well, 6-well, and 10 cm plates are suitable for mESCs/miPSC plating.
Add 2 ml of 0.1% gelatin into the well of a 6-well plate.
Swirl to cover the entire surface with the gelatin solution.
Take the frozen inactivated MEF vial from the liquid nitrogen tank.
Thaw the vial in the 37°C thermo heater.
Spray the outside of the vial with 70% ethanol to sterilize and place it in hood.
Add pre-warmed 1 mL FM10 media into the MEF and pipet the thawed cells gently.
Transfer the mixture into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add 8 mL FM10 medium to the cell suspension, making a total of 10 mL.
Remove 100 μL of cell suspension for counting the cells.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 4 minutes.
Mix 100 μL of cell suspension with an equal volume of Trypan Blue by gentle pipetting.
Fill both sides of the counting slide with approximately 10 μL of the mixed cell and Trypan Blue solution.
Count cells using an automated cell counter to determine total cell number and concentration of viable and non-viable cells.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cell suspension.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed FM10 medium to the pellet.
Transfer the mixture into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add another 23 mL of pre-warmed FM10 medium to achieve a final concentration of 1.2 × 10^5 cells/mL.
Aspirate the gelatin from the 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL MEF containing FM10 media to each well (containing 2.5 × 10^5 cells/well).
Incubate overnight in an incubator, leaving the plate for at least 4 hours up to 24 hours.
Plate inactivated MEFs at a density of 0.3 × 10^5 cells/cm² for at least 4 hours, preferably up to 72 hours before plating ESCs or iPSCs.
Allow MEFs to attach and spread completely to cover the dish surface.
Do not use MEF feeder layer more than 4 days after plating.
Gelatinize plates with 0.1% gelatin for at least 20 minutes in an incubator before plating ESCs or iPSCs.
Take the frozen vial from the liquid nitrogen tank.
Put the vial on dry ice.
Thaw the vial in a thermo heater.
Add pre-warmed 1 mL FM10 media to the thawed cells.
Centrifuge the cell mixture at 200 × g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 2–3 mL of pre-warmed t2i/L media.
Aspirate MEF media from a prepared 6-well plate.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for at least 4 hours.
Add t2i/L media containing mESCs/miPSCs to the plate.
Incubate the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2, and 95% humidity incubator for 24 hours.
After 24 hours of incubation, observe the status of mESCs/miPSCs under a microscope.
Aspirate the t2i/L media.
Add 2–3 mL t2i/L media every 24 hours.
Check cell conditions and change the t2i/L medium with 2–3 mL fresh t2i/L medium every 24 hours.
When cells reach 80%–90% confluence, passage the cells into another well.
Aspirate the t2i/L media for passage.
Add 2 mL pre-warmed PBS and wash out the culture medium completely in one step.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin.
Use Accutase to disperse mESCs/miPSCs in the incubator for 4 minutes.
Check trypsin digestion by tapping the plate and observing cell detachment under microscope.
Aspirate FM10 media from MEF-plated well.
Add 2–3 mL pre-warmed t2i/L media.
Take trypsinized mESCs/miPSCs well from incubator after 4 minutes.
Add 1 ml t2i/L media to the cell mixture.
Pipette thoroughly with a 1000 μL pipetman and separate each cell.
Transfer cell mixture into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add another 8 ml FM10 medium (total 10 ml) and mix well with a 10 ml pipette.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving a small amount of medium.
Pipette thoroughly with a 200 μL pipetman to separate each cell.
Add 1 ml pre-warmed t2i/L medium and mix thoroughly with a 1000 μL pipetman.
Count the cell number.
Take the cell-containing media (1 × 10^5 cells) and transfer into the MEF-plated 6-well plate.
Gently move the wells approximately twice in forward-backward and left-right while maintaining a horizontal position to allow mESCs/miPSCs to be evenly distributed.
Leave the well in the incubator overnight (12–24 h).
Replace the medium with t2i/L medium.
Add 2 mL pre-warmed PBS and wash out the culture medium in one step.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin.
Leave it for 4 min in the incubator.
Dissociate cells into a single-cell suspension by vigorous pipetting.
Add 1 mL t2i/L media.
Count the cell number.
Take the cell-containing media (1 × 10^6 cells) for transfection.
Dissociate cells completely into single cells.
Use a 30–40 μm strainer to ensure complete dissociation if necessary.
Mix pellets with 3 μg of transposase-expressing vector.
Add 3 μg of the piggyBac transposon gene expression vector (pPB-CAG-mZscan5b-P2A-EGFP).
Combine the mixture with 100 μL Opti-MEM media.
Transfect miPSCs by electroporation using NEPA21 under specified conditions.
Apply poring pulse: 125 V, 5 ms-pulse width, 50 ms pulse interval, two pulses, 10% attenuation rate.
Apply transfer pulse: 20 V, 50 ms pulse width, 50 ms pulse interval, five pulses, 40% attenuation rate.
Move the piggyBac transposon gene expression vector into the cytoplasm with a few transfer pulses using low voltage and long duration after poring pulse.
Prepare a fresh working solution for injection by mixing reagents 30 min before each time point.
Plate electroporated cells onto a 6-well MEF plate in mouse t2i/L medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a cuvette for electroporation.
Apply poring pulse: 125 V, 5 ms-pulse width, 50 ms pulse interval, two pulses, 10% attenuation rate, +.
Apply transfer pulse: 20 V, 50 ms pulse width, 50 ms pulse interval, five pulses, 40% attenuation rate, +/-.
Plate the electroporated cells onto a 6-well MEF plate in mouse t2i/L medium.
Grasp both ends of the glass capillary and scald it with fire.
Pull the capillary to both ends after leaving it for 1-2 s.
Heat and cut the center when the capillary is stretched.
The tip of the needle curls into a hook shape caused by the force of the rising heat.
Cut the end of the needle with a ruby pen by making a slit.
Finalize the product after cutting with a ruby pen.
In a single motion, remove the pipette from the flame and pull on each end gently and quickly to draw out a thin filament before glass hardens.
Begin several inches above the flame and slowly move the thin drawn part of the filament down towards the flame to pull a very fine filament.
Pull a second time to form a fine needle end on the tip of the pipette.
Pass the fine end quickly over the top of the flame to curl the tip into a hook.
Ensure the hooked end is thin enough for microdissection but thick enough to withstand pressure.
Discard tools immediately after use in an appropriate glass tool waste receptacle.
Set the pore size of the pipette to less than 100 μm (50–70 μm).
Identify GFP-positive colonies under a fluorescence microscope for mESC/miPSC colony picking after transfection.
Transfection efficiency of electroporation should be around 20%.
Change the medium in the well to be passaged and on the feeders before microdissection.
Wash the new feeders once with appropriate solution.
Add 2 mL t2i/L medium (6-well plate) on the new feeders.
Keep the feeders in the incubator during dissection.
Maintain an optimal environment by utilizing a humidified 5% CO2/20% O2 mixed gas source and a warm plate.
Use fluorescence microscopy to find an ideal colony of small, round, randomly organized cells with a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio that have not yet begun to form structures within the colony.
Circle the bottom of the dish with the identified colony using a pen.
Bring a stereomicroscope into a laminar flow hood.
Peel off the whole colony and incubate it in 0.25% trypsin (100 μL drop).
Pipette and microdissect chunks of approximately 100 cells using glass hooks.
Swirl the cell chunks into the center of the dish after micro-dissection.
Transfer 20 to 50 chunks to new feeder wells in a small-diameter 4-well dish using a micropipette.
Pre-coat the micropipette tip with t2i/L medium to prevent cells from sticking.
Leave the dishes for 24 hours to allow the cell chunks to attach to the dish.
Exchange the medium, providing 0.5 mL per well.
Aspirate t2i/L culture media from mESC/miPSC culture dishes.
Add 0.5 mL (for 12-well) or 1 mL (for 6-well) of 0.25% Trypsin.
Incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Neutralize with an equal volume of FM10 media.
Transfer the dissociated cells to a 15 mL Falcon tube and bring up to 10 mL with FM10 media.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 4 min.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cell pellet in PBS medium (volume depends on the cell number).
Aspirate the t2i/L media from transfected mESCs/miPSCs cultures.
Add 2 mL pre-warmed PBS and wash out the culture medium in one step.
Aspirate the PBS.
Add 1 mL pre-warmed 0.25% Trypsin to the cells and leave it for 4 min in the incubator.
Take the MEF-plated well (not yet mESCs/miPSCs plated).
Aspirate media from the MEF-plated well.
Add 2–3 mL pre-warmed t2i/L media to the MEF-plated well.
After 4 min, take the trypsin-plated well from the incubator.
Add 1 mL FM10 media to the cells in the well.
Pipette with a 1000 μL pipet thoroughly and separate each cell using filter tips.
Transfer the mixture into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add another 8 mL FM10 medium, and mix well with a 10 mL pipette.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 4 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL pre-warmed FM10 medium.
Pipette thoroughly with a 1000 μL pipetman to separate each cell.
Count the cell number.
Take 100 μL (1:10) of cell-containing medium (1 × 10^5 cells).
Transfer into the MEF-plated well of a 6-well plate.
Shake the mESCs/miPSC well so that cells can be plated uniformly across the well.
Incubate overnight (12–24 hours).
Replace the medium with t2i/L medium.
